summary: Blits a 24-bit RGB image with transparent-color support. A global stores the transparent color (a7 masked to 24 bits) and a global stores the scanline byte width (3 * a5). When the transparent color is 0xFFFFFF the fast path copies whole scanlines with qmemcpy; otherwise each scanline copies pixels individually, skipping any pixel equal to the transparent color. Source and destination rows advance by precomputed stride differences after each scanline.

operations.description: Store the transparent color from the last argument masked to 24 bits: dword_5DD804 = a7 & 0xFFFFFF.
Store the scanline byte width: dword_5DD814 = 3 * a5.
Compute per-row advance past the copied region for source (v17 = a2 - 3 * a5) and destination (v18 = a4 - 3 * a5).
Branch on whether the transparent color (a7 & 0xFFFFFF) equals 0xFFFFFF: selects the bulk-copy path vs the per-pixel path.
Fast path: for each scanline, qmemcpy dword_5DD814 bytes from source to destination, then advance both pointers by the copied width plus the stored row advance.
Slow path: for each scanline, copy a5 pixels one at a time; advance source and destination by their row-advance values at the end of the scanline.
Reconstruct one 24-bit pixel: read the low 16 bits from the word at source offset 0, shift, and read the third byte at source offset 2.
If the reconstructed pixel differs from the stored transparent color, write the pixel as a 32-bit value at the destination; advance the destination by 3 bytes per pixel.
Both paths iterate per scanline using a countdown on the row-count argument; loop continues while the countdown has not reached 1.
